steps.text: Cook ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat until evenly browned and crumbly, 7 to 8 minutes. Remove from the heat and sprinkle flour over top; stir until beef is evenly coated and all fat is absorbed.

Return the skillet to the stove over medium heat. Stir in 2 cups milk; cook and stir until warm and beginning to thicken, 3 to 5 minutes. Add remaining 2 cups milk; cook and stir until desired consistency has been reached and gravy comes to a boil, about 5 minutes. Season with onion salt, salt, and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Hamburger Gravy
raw_recipe.description: This hamburger gravy recipe uses pan drippings, flour, and milk to create a thick, meaty gravy you can serve over noodles, mashed potatoes, or biscuits.
raw_recipe.name: Hamburger Gravy

review.reviewBody: Not a bad recipe. Easy to make...easy to spice up. I really like the idea of mixing the flour with the hamburger first. I added the onion soup mix, the worchester (?) sauce, some garlic, and no-salt extra seasonings. The recipe by itself may be a little bland as one of the reviews stated but cooking, I believe, is the art of creation. Out of chaos can come beauty!!!

Knowing from previous reviews, I did tweak and add. I chopped up an onion and garlic. Added seasonings and even put some worcestershire sauce and A1 to the the bowl while I was preparing other steps. I used beef broth to the hamburger and used it to make the jasmine rice. At the end, I added the rice to the "gravy" and mixed. As mentioned prior, it is a good base to be creative. I meant to get mushrooms. You could add frozen mixed veggies. The meal was a hearty dinner.

Ugh, such a comforting meal! My mom made this countless times when I was growing up, always a family favourite. I sauteed a small onion in some butter to start until it was cooked down, then added some fresh garlic. Cooked the beef, added salt and pepper and then drained the meat. After adding the flour and milk I did add a beef bouillon cube for more flavour as other users suggested and then more salt and pepper to taste. It turned out absolutely delicious! We had it over mashed potatoes with butter, sour cream, chives, milk, garlic powder salt and pepper :-) will definitely be making this again and again

Made this for dinner 2night and the kids & I LOVED it, even my finicky 3 & 1/2 year old found no fault with it and my 18 month old son gobbled it up as did his father when he got home. Not one speck was left! 

Now I did tweek slightly, I cooked 1 Lb gr beef with 1 onion diced (though this was not mentioned in the directions I am sure that was what was intended since it is listed in the ingredients) and 3 cloves garlic crushed. I added lots of fresh ground pepper and kosher salt & slightly more flour and more milk in hopes this would be left overs for lunch, LOL- until my husband ate it ALL!!

My husbands grandmother cooked this when he was young but a very fatty version. I leaned it up with very lean ground beef. First I sautee, onion, crushed garlic in a small amount of grape seed oil, then i add the meat and season. My favorite to season this is McCormicks steak seasoning, once browned, add whole wheat flour to skim milk, add to the meat then we have found that is very good over brown rice instead of potatoes.

Made this with Jimmy Dean's maple sausage which gave it so much flavor! Only had a lb of sausage so only needed 2 cups of milk. My husband loved it more than the package gravy and even my 2 yo, who hates biscuits and gravy, had 2 servings!! I'll never buy the packaged gravy again!

The original recipe is a good base. Here are the additions I made and came out very tasty. Approved by a teen, a toddler, and husband:
-One whole onion chopped and cooked with meat (instead of onion powder)
-3 cloves minced garlic (instead of garlic powder) added to meat when it was almost done
-1.5 tsp pepper
-1.5 tsp beef better than boullion 
-0.5 - 1 tsp all purpose seasoning. 

We will be making it again! Good for a night you don't have much time. We did it over garlic mashed potatoes this round, but will try over egg noodles next time.
This recipe was easy and awesome I did make it my own and used heavy cream sautés some onion white and green, garlic ,and mushrooms together. Then, put it over some rice yummy!!
I've been making this for years. However I drain the fat off of the meat, make gravy, add to it onion, garlic, grated carrot, diced sweet peppers. Served over mashed potatoes.

This is good if you have hamburger meat defrosted and don't really know what to do with it hahaha this is what I did: brown the meat drained it added onion and red and green bell peppers, then 1/4cup of flour with about 1/2 pint of whipping cream 1/4 cup of milk added Worcestershire sauce (1/2cup) then pepper, creole seasoning, accent' flavoring, liquid beef broth about a cup and let it simmer. Came out amazing!!! I like to season according to mood when I cook hahahaa OH! spoon it over fresh mashed potatoes....mmmmm

This is pretty much the same recipe I use when I make this. Sometimes I add a few cloves of chopped garlic and or garlic powder (we love garlic! lol) and a finely diced onion to the meat while i brown it. Also I don't like to use that much milk so most of my liquid comes from draining the potatoes. A good tip - you should use quite a bit of salt if serving over potatoes. Add salt until the point that you think it is just about too much. You want the meat to be quite salty because the potatoes will need it.
Added minced onion and seasoning it was tasty on a rainy day.
The only change I made was to put in actual onions instead of onion powder since I like them. Great recipe.
Using a touch of Kitchen Bouquet will give it a more appealing color.

This is a great springboard for personal expression. I love to turn it into a simple and quick hamburger "Stroganoff ". Just add some Worchestershire sauce and sour cream. Sautéed mushrooms bring it up another notch.
We call this SOS
Hmm. Put this over toast and it's a dead ringer for Army SOS. In order to make it palatable in those days, we added Tabasco sauce, if you could find it. Gotta say, it kept one going....and going...
Been making this for over 20 years when there is leftover ground beef from ?hamburgers, meatloaf? what ever. But love the idea of mixing the flour and meat -no lumps

You can do so much more with this recipe. Throw in some garlic powder and onion powder or a packet of onion soup mix, salt and pepper on that burger as it cooks and then once you do the flour and milk throw in some sour cream or cream cheese. You could even add a can of cream chicken soup instead of using the flour and milk. I like to add cooked green peas to my gravy before I put it over the taters.

Thought it was rather bland but I put in a little toco spices, diced onion and 1 clove garlic diced and it tasted better. Oh, instead of flour I used cornstarch. I think it works better for making gravy.
